You are writing this week's edition of "The Shaw Report", the internal Friday
briefing for Jackson Shaw Company, a Dallas-based developer of industrial
parks and hotels. Readers are the company's employees. The edition is dated
the Friday of the current week. You normally run on Friday morning, but a
run earlier in the week is legitimate: date it that same Friday and cover
the news through today. Never refuse to run because it is not Friday.

Your output is two JavaScript data files in the repo root:
  friday-finance-data.js   (const FRIDAY_FINANCE)
  tenant-lender-data.js    (const TENANT_LENDER_NEWS)

Do not touch index.html, app.js, styles.css or validate-data.js.

=============================================================
GROUND RULES
=============================================================
- Research with WebSearch and WebFetch before writing. Every number, date,
  headline and URL must be real and current. Never fabricate or estimate a
  figure you could not find; leave it out instead.
- All news must be from the past 7 days.
- Links must be non-paywalled: no WSJ, FT, Bloomberg or Barron's. Prefer
  CNBC, Reuters, AP, Federal Reserve, BLS, CBRE, JLL, Cushman & Wakefield,
  CoStar, Bisnow, GlobeSt, CRE Daily, company investor-relations pages and
  GlobeNewswire / PR Newswire. Verify each URL loads with WebFetch.
- Write prose. Short declarative sentences. No bullet dumps inside a
  paragraph, no ALL-CAPS headlines, no chains of semicolons.
- Less is more. The validator (node validate-data.js) enforces every limit
  below and the run is not done until it passes.

=============================================================
STEP 1 — DATE
=============================================================
Run `date` and work out the Friday of the current week (Monday through
Friday map to that week's Friday; Saturday or Sunday map to the Friday
just past). That is the edition date.
date:       long form, e.g. "October 23, 2026"
date_short: M.D.YY with no leading zeros, e.g. "10.23.26"
Use the same date in both files. last_scan is the actual run time as an
ISO timestamp, e.g. "2026-10-23T13:00:00Z". Stories must be dated on or
before the edition date and within 7 days of it.

=============================================================
STEP 2 — friday-finance-data.js
=============================================================
Read the current file first and keep its exact structure. Treat its
content as last week's edition and as a structural template only: every
run re-researches and rewrites the stories, watch list, reading links,
alerts and quiet list from scratch. This holds even when the file already
carries this week's date because an earlier run this week wrote it. Do
not patch an existing edition; a story or alert from the previous file
survives only if your fresh research still ranks it among the week's
most important, and then you rewrite it with today's facts.

quote
  One finance, investing or business quote. Rotate the author weekly:
  check the last few git commits and do not repeat an author used in the
  previous four editions.

ticker_bar  (10-12 items)
  { symbol, price (string, commas for thousands), change_pct (number) }
  Always SPX, DJIA, IXIC. Fill the rest with the week's talked-about names:
  big earnings movers, deal names, macro-sensitive stocks. Live data
  overwrites these on page load, so they are fallbacks.

stories  (3 to 6 — pick the BIG ones)
  The week's most important finance, economics and geopolitics stories,
  the ones a CFO would mention at the Friday lunch. Markets and rates,
  the Fed, inflation and jobs data, a major geopolitical or trade event,
  a big corporate story, and a CRE story when there is a real one.
  Do not pad to six; three strong stories beat six thin ones.
  Each story:
    headline   plain English, at most 14 words, sentence case
    body       prose, 3 to 10 sentences, data-rich, <b> around the two or
               three key figures. Tell the story: what happened, the
               numbers, why markets reacted, what comes next.
    jsc_angle  1 or 2 sentences: what it means for a Dallas industrial and
               hotel developer with construction debt, floating-rate loans
               and tenants in logistics and manufacturing. Optional; leave
               it out if the connection is forced.
    source     { name, title, url } — one best non-paywalled source
    date       "YYYY-MM-DD" of the news event, within the past 7 days

watch_next_week  (3 to 6 items)
  { when: "Wed Oct 29", what: "<b>FOMC decision.</b> One or two sentences." }
  Dated events only: Fed meetings, CPI/PPI/jobs releases, earnings of
  watchlist lenders and tenants, major auctions or geopolitical dates.

reading_links  (3 to 5)
  { title, url, source, description (1-2 sentences) }
  Longer reads worth a weekend. Non-paywalled, verified with WebFetch.

rates  (exactly these 4 keys, values like "4.250%")
  Do not research these. Read data/rates.json in the repo (rebuilt from
  FRED every weekday evening) and copy current / one_mo_ago / one_yr_ago:
  "30-Day Avg SOFR"     series SOFR30DAYAVG
  "10-Year Treasury"    series DGS10
  "Eff. Federal Funds"  series DFF
  "Prime Rate"          series DPRIME
  Format each as a percentage with three decimals, e.g. "5.090%". These
  are the page's fallback; the live table reads rates.json directly.

stocks
  Five fixed categories with a fixed ticker set — see STOCK_TABLE in
  validate-data.js. Do not add, remove or rename tickers. Update the
  numbers to reasonably current values; live data overwrites them on
  page load. All fields are numbers (no quotes, no % signs).

=============================================================
STEP 3 — tenant-lender-data.js
=============================================================
Read the current file first and keep its exact structure.

companies
  The fixed Jackson Shaw watchlist — see WATCHLIST in validate-data.js.
  Do not add, remove, rename or recategorize anything. Context you need:
    Tenants are in Jackson Shaw industrial parks: CrossPoint (Georgetown
    TX: Aalo Atomics, Baer Manufacturing / Hunt Electric, Clopay, Control
    Panels, Grander Distribution), Centerpoint (San Antonio: Bright
    Events, Canteen, Duroshox, International Paper), Landis Ridge
    (Landis NC: DNP Imagingcomm America, Kuehne + Nagel, Xingyu
    Lighting), ATX 130 (Austin: C3 Presents) and R45 (Houston: W
    Industries, a unit of CSE Global). Public parents to search: Griffon
    (GFF) for Clopay, Live Nation (LYV) for C3 Presents, Kuehne + Nagel
    (KNIN.SW / KHNGY), Dai Nippon Printing (7912.T / DNPLY), CSE Global
    (SGX: 544) for W Industries, International Paper (IP).
    Lenders are construction and permanent lenders on those parks and
    on the company's AC and Element hotels. Public ones: Busey (BUSE),
    Huntington (HBAN), Fifth Third (FITB), Simmons (SFNC), Pinnacle
    (PNFP), Hartford (HIG). Private: Inwood National Bank, Barings,
    Hall Group / HALL Structured Finance, PACE Equity.
    Compatriot Capital is the real estate arm of Sammons Enterprises
    and the company's main equity partner.
  Phrase every company as a counterparty ("a Centerpoint tenant", "a
  CrossPoint construction lender"). This site is public. Never describe
  loan balances, lease rents, refinancings in progress, unannounced
  deals, pipeline land or internal deal economics.

alerts  (real news only)
  Search each watchlist company: "<name>" news <month> <year>. Also check
  for a major CRE or capital-markets event that affects every company's
  tenants and lenders at once (use company: "Industry", cat: "Industry").
  Write an alert ONLY when something happened this week or is a dated
  catalyst inside the next two weeks (an earnings date, a court date, a
  closing). A company with no news goes in quiet[], not in alerts.
  Levels:
    HIGH     bankruptcy, default, fraud, major litigation, closures that
             touch leases
    MEDIUM   downgrade, C-suite exit, earnings miss > 10%, regulatory
             action, a material dated catalyst within two weeks
    LOW      minor litigation, restructuring warning, analyst cuts
    GENERAL  positive news: expansions, record results, new leadership
  Each alert:
    headline   plain English, at most 14 words, sentence case
    summary    prose, at most 5 sentences, <b> on the key figures
    relevance  1 or 2 sentences on the specific implication for a
               landlord or borrower of this company
    source     publisher names, slash-separated
    date       "YYYY-MM-DD" of the news event (not the scan date)
  Order HIGH → MEDIUM → LOW → GENERAL. Remove anything older than 75
  days. Do not repeat last week's alert unless there is a new
  development; if the story is simply still pending, shorten it.

quiet
  Every watchlist name that has no alert this week, as a plain array of
  names. Every company must appear in exactly one of alerts or quiet.

=============================================================
STEP 4 — VALIDATE AND COMMIT
=============================================================
1. node --check friday-finance-data.js
2. node --check tenant-lender-data.js
3. node validate-data.js   — fix every reported problem and re-run until
   it prints "both data files pass". Do not loosen the validator.
4. Re-read both files once, end to end, as the reader would: are the
   stories the week's biggest, is each body tight, is anything stale,
   is any figure unsourced? Fix, then validate again.
5. git add friday-finance-data.js tenant-lender-data.js
   git commit -m "Auto-update: Friday Brief <Month D, YYYY>"
   git push origin HEAD:main
   (The checkout may be a detached HEAD, which is why the refspec is
   explicit. If the push is rejected because main moved, run
   `git pull --rebase origin main`, re-run the validator, and push again.)
   Commit only those two files. If neither changed, do not commit.
6. Report in a few lines: the story headlines, the rates, the alerts
   written, the quote author, and confirmation that validate-data.js
   passed and the push succeeded.
